court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: III Additional Family Court, Chennai - O.P.No.2864 of 2009
facts_of_case: The respondent filed for dissolution of marriage under Section 13(1)(i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, read with Section 7 of the Family Courts Act, 1986. The appellant suffered physical defects and the respondent's parents were depressed due to suppression. The couple did not have a cordial relationship within 10 days of marriage.

legal_principles.principle: The restriction of one year contained in Section 14 of the Hindu Marriage Act is only directory and not mandatory.
legal_principles.held: Firstly, the Act did not contain any provision for consequences of non-compliance of time limit prescribed in Section 14. Secondly, as per the proviso to Section 14, the Court has power to permit the petitioner to file petition before expiry of one year on the application of the petitioner claiming exceptional hardship or exceptional depravity on the part of the respondent.
cited_cases: S.Gugan Vs. R.Nisha, SCC Online Mad 17063

legal_principles.principle: A petition can be filed before lapse of one year of date of marriage by obtaining permission from the Court.
legal_principles.held: This permission can be obtained even after filing a petition for dissolution of marriage.
cited_cases: S.Gugan Vs. R.Nisha, SCC Online Mad 17063

outcome.final_order: The trial court decree and judgment dated 17.12.2014 were confirmed, and the appeal was dismissed.

use_for_drafting: assisting with Hindu Marriage Act cases
